capabilities.target: External company enrichment API, billed per call, shared monthly quota
Researcher sub-agent investigating one CRM account
CRM account record: industry, size, headquarters fields

inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows to enrich
Open-ended research content gathered by spawned researcher sub-agents while 'investigating' an account; the prompt names no source allowlist or tool restriction for this research

instructions.note: 'Keep going until every row is complete' sets no bound on retries, spawned sub-agents, spend, or runtime, directly enabling unbounded cost and recursive spawning.
'If a lookup fails or looks incomplete' gives no objective completeness criterion, so the ~3 percent of rows with malformed company names can never satisfy it and will loop indefinitely.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota, shared with sales and marketing teams
Sales and marketing tools that depend on the same shared API key and quota

controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; runtime notes state there is no spend alert and no maximum on calls.

controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; runtime notes explicitly state there is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

findings.title: Lethal spend loop (TC6): unbounded retries and recursive sub-agent spawning on malformed rows drain the shared enrichment quota and disrupt sales/marketing tools

attack_path.note: Nightly batch includes roughly 3 percent (about 1,200 of 40,000) rows with malformed company names that never return a complete lookup result.
Prompt instructs retrying failed or incomplete lookups with no retry cap; each retry is a billed call against the shared quota.
Prompt also allows spawning a researcher sub-agent per stuck row, and sub-agents can recursively spawn their own researchers, with no depth or count limit.
Unbounded retries and recursive spawning consume the shared monthly API quota faster than intended, with no spend alert to catch it.
Once the shared quota is exhausted, sales and marketing tools that depend on the same key stop working until the next month.

evidence.observation: There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents; sub agents can spawn their own researchers, creating an unbounded recursive branching factor.
enrich.lookup is billed per call on an API key and monthly quota shared with sales and marketing; when the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month.
Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000 row nightly batch (about 1,200 rows) have malformed company names that never return a complete result, guaranteeing the retry/spawn condition fires every night.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account, so an overrun would not be noticed until the shared quota is already exhausted.
'retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent... Keep going until every row is complete' contains no retry limit, spawn limit, or termination condition for unresolvable rows.

recommendations.action: Cap retries per row (for example 3) and cap sub-agent spawn depth and count per row and per run; mark unresolved rows as needing manual review instead of retrying indefinitely.
Add a hard spend cap or circuit breaker on the enrichment API client that halts the batch when a per-run cost threshold is reached.
Add real-time spend and usage alerting on the shared enrichment account so an overrun is caught before quota exhaustion.
Issue the enrichment agent its own API key and quota, isolated from the shared key used by sales and marketing tools.

findings.title: Untrusted research findings written into CRM as fact via spawned researcher sub-agents

attack_path.note: Researcher sub-agents are spawned to 'investigate the account' for rows where enrich.lookup fails or looks incomplete, implying open-ended external research with no declared source restriction.
The sub-agent runs with no scope limit on what sources it may consult or what it treats as the answer.
Whatever the researcher concludes is written back into CRM industry, size, and headquarters fields with no validation or provenance check described.

evidence.observation: 'spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate the account' implies open-ended research with no stated source allowlist or trust boundary on what the researcher may consult.
No limits on sub-agent behavior or recursive spawning are declared, and no output validation step is mentioned before the write to CRM.

recommendations.action: Require the researcher sub-agent to cite verifiable sources and route its proposed field values through a validation or review step before cap.crm_write executes.
Tag CRM fields written by researcher sub-agents with provenance such as model-derived and unverified, so downstream consumers do not treat them as equivalent to verified data.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach critical inherent risk: an A4 fully autonomous agent that can spawn recursive sub-agents (cap.spawn_researcher) and make unbounded billed calls (cap.enrich_lookup) against a shared, un-metered quota satisfies the autonomy modifier on an S3 sink (f1), and the same unbounded spawning feeding an unvalidated write of untrusted research into CRM satisfies it on an S2 sink (f2). No structural control in the design (retry/spawn limit, spend cap, spend alert, quota isolation, or output validation) is declared or verified; every identified control is missing_recommended and earns no credit under rubric section 5, so residual equals inherent for both findings. No forecast-horizon findings were raised because the paths are fully open today with no controls left to decay; forecast equals residual. The single highest-leverage fix is adding a hard spend cap and retry/spawn limit (ctl.step_spawn_limit, ctl.spend_cap), since the 3 percent malformed-row rate against a 40,000-row nightly batch makes the spend loop almost certain to trigger on every run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest or MCP/API configuration was provided for enrich.lookup or the researcher sub-agent; capability scope, especially what the researcher sub-agent is permitted to query, is inferred from the system prompt, so confidence on finding f2 is medium.
No credential scope or IaC documentation was provided for cap.crm_write; its credential_scope is recorded as unknown.
The exact branching factor and cost of recursive sub-agent spawning could not be quantified without runtime logs; the attack path is described qualitatively.
